npm_note: The structural difference from the zai lane: this lane rides opencode on the ANTHROPIC protocol, zai on OpenAI-compatible. The field exists precisely so that difference is DATA and not a second code path.
endpoint_note: The subscription (Kimi Code membership) endpoint. The vendor's own warning, verbatim: "Kimi Code membership benefits and the Kimi Platform have different Base URLs. Please ensure your Base URL and API Key are matched correctly." HONEST LIMIT: unlike Z.AI, Moonshot does NOT publish what a membership key does when sent to the metered endpoint (audit U5) — the separation is documented, the failure mode is not. Nothing here claims a guarantee the vendor never made.

recorded_endpoints.note: The international metered Kimi Open Platform endpoint. Recorded so the endpoint self-check owns the wrong-endpoint case by name; never wired.

credential.note: A broker engine-cred auth-profile NAME plus the variable its spawn-time injection fills. The variable name was READ OFF the installed opencode 1.18.3 provider record for `kimi-for-coding` on 2026-08-24 ($0, local, no live provider call) — never guessed; the audit's U-register left it unverified because models.dev's page carried no env field. The material is resolved fresh at spawn and never stored, logged, or persisted.

data_policy.statement: The kimi lane carries a no-household-personal-data routing constraint. It is approved for code and general technical work only; household personal data, personal correspondence, and identity-bearing content must never route to it.
data_policy.basis: Operating entity 北京月之暗面科技有限公司 (Beijing Moonshot AI); personal information stored within mainland China; training on inputs is the DEFAULT with only a contact-based opt-out; no GDPR/EEA language. Governing law differs between the two applicable agreements (Singapore for OpenPlatform, PRC for the assistant property) and no page states which binds a membership (audit U6) — the constraint is written to hold under either reading.
data_policy.enforcement_note: RECORDED AND SURFACED, NOT MACHINE-ENFORCED. No per-lane data-policy enforcement point exists in the tree as of 2026-08-24 (grep-verified at P3-LN-3); enforcement lands with the routing-policy seam, and this row is what that seam will read. The rider needs an AFFIRMATIVE operator answer at the gate, not merely an absence of objection.

model_routing_note: TIER GATE, NOT REGION GATE. Kimi's model gate is by MEMBERSHIP TIER, not by region, so region_model_gate stays "none" on every row. The tier gate is real and enforced on the wire — 401 "Your current subscription does not have access to k3" — and the thing that handles it is the model-list-diff canary (P-T17-3), not a new attribute. Do not invent a tier_model_gate field.
overflow_note: overflow_mode is `opt-in-credits` on every model: the Extra Usage Credit Pack is OFF by default, requires funding, and carries an explicitly PROVEN disable (satisfying 3.10 / P-T17-2), verbatim: "You can turn it off at any time: your balance stays in your account and the system pauses spending from it; turn it back on to resume." RECOMMENDED OPERATOR POSTURE: Extra Usage OFF, under which the lane behaves as a hard stop and the ¥-denominated top-up rails are moot. Turning it on is a deliberate, reversible operator act through the rehearsed kill-switch operation — never automatic, never silent.

reasoning_effort.note: K3 documents thinking efforts but NO disable, so the Z.AI thinking:{type:disabled} lever has no Kimi equivalent and no eco_options are declared. THE VALUE LIST IS UNVERIFIED AT PRIMARY SOURCE — PROVENANCE: the packet brief, NOT the audit, which records no effort vocabulary for this model at all. It is carried unwired and dated precisely so nothing is built on it; the ceremony or the operator's console closes it. Recorded as a dated unwired fact rather than wiring an S10.6 rung nothing sanctions.

installed_catalogue_record.source: the installed opencode 1.18.3 provider catalogue — models.dev data the ENGINE fetches at boot into its per-user cache (the npm package `opencode-ai@1.18.3` ships no such file; verified by inspecting the installed package). Read locally, $0, no live provider call.
installed_catalogue_record.agrees: provider id `kimi-for-coding`; npm `@ai-sdk/anthropic`; base URL `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1`; env var `KIMI_API_KEY`; and ALL FOUR model ids this document declares — k3, k3-256k, kimi-for-coding, kimi-for-coding-highspeed. No declared id is absent from the installed record.
installed_catalogue_record.diverges: The catalogue's DISPLAY NAME for model `kimi-for-coding` is "Kimi K2.7 Code", where this document carries "Kimi For Coding" from the vendor's own product docs. Recorded as a dated discrepancy rather than silently resolved, exactly as the `/coding/` vs `/coding/v1` Anthropic-base divergence above is — the id is what dispatches, the name is cosmetic, and the account's observed list is the authority (P-T17-3).
installed_catalogue_record.additional: The catalogue also publishes per-model context limits the audit did not capture (k3 1,048,576; k3-256k, kimi-for-coding and kimi-for-coding-highspeed 262,144) and prices every model at $0.00 — the S03.7 corollary, so this lane's dollars come from Sinet's own metered rows and NEVER from the engine.
installed_catalogue_record.note: The catalogue is a SEED like everything else here. It is the installed engine's own record, which makes it authoritative over documentation for what the engine will accept, and still not authoritative over the ACCOUNT, whose observed model list the model-list canary reads.

reset_marker_note: DELIBERATELY EMPTY. The audit found no documented reset-time signal (U4): the error reference publishes no reset timestamp and states reset times live in the Console. signals_note: DOCUMENTED-NOT-OBSERVED. Every row below is a MESSAGE STRING quoted from the vendor's published error reference on 2026-08-24, not a body observed on the wire: the audit could not verify the actual JSON shape of a Kimi error body, whether it carries a code field, or whether any reset header exists (U3/U4/U5). The key ceremony's live single-request probe must capture one real 401, one real 429 and — if reachable — one real 403 body before this table is treated as final. The P-T17-1 auth canary is the authoritative revocation detector for whatever the message grammar misses.
